newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka says Tamil rebels killed in attack.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka says Tamil rebels killed in attack.

text.p: Several Tamil rebels were believed killed when government forces launched air, naval and artillery strikes on rebel jungle bases in Sri Lanka's northeast on Thursday, a military spokesman said on Friday.
"The strike is now over. It was a limited operation," military spokesman Brigadier Tissa Jayatunga told Reuters.
"We believe there were many casualties to the LTTE (Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam), but we don't have confirmation of numbers yet," he said.
The attacks were centred on the LTTE's so-called "14 base" complex in the jungles of northeastern Mullaitivu district, 280 km (175 miles) from the capital Colombo, military officials said.
"LTTE camps in the area were pounded for three or four hours starting at dawn," an official said. Bases for the rebels' Sea Tiger naval wing were also attacked.
The LTTE claimed late on Thursday that concentrated shelling of northeast coastal villages by Sri Lankan naval boats had killed at least one fisherman and wounded several.
The clandestine Voice of Tiger radio, monitored in the northern town of Vavuniya, said the Sri Lankan navy had fired shells at residential areas between Alampil and Salai villages.
The radio said hundreds of fishermen were displaced in the shelling and were forced to move to safer areas.
It did not report any rebel casualties.
LTTE rebels overran a key military base in the area last year, killing or capturing more than 1,000 soldiers in the army's worst setback of the war, now in its 14th year.
Jayatunga said the aim of Thursday's offensive was to destroy all known rebel bases in the Mullaitivu jungles and along the eastern seaboard.
Several camps in the base complex and others on the coast were destroyed, he said.
An LTTE spokesman in London confirmed the attack but said the Sri Lankan military shelled Tamil villages and not rebel camps.
"This is not an attack on any LTTE base at all. This is a deliberate attack on Tamil villages in the area by the armed forces," Anton Rajah told Reuters by telephone.
"It is feared many human lives have been lost but further information on casualties is not immeditely available."
Thursday's attack by the military came after the LTTE overran an army detachment in the eastern Batticaloa district last week, killing at least 65 soldiers.
The military said at least 200 rebels were killed in the raid.
The LTTE are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's north and east.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war. The LTTE says the number is higher.
